audience: Healthy youth footballers in team age groups U5-U17
contentNote: These are original PureAthletic routine outlines informed by the linked source principles. They are not copied sessions and are not medical, rehabilitation, or return-to-play advice.

routines.title: Match-day ball confidence
routines.purpose: Build familiar touches and confidence without creating fatigue before a game.

blocks.title: Ball hello
activities: Move freely with the ball and try inside, outside, and sole touches.
When the adult calls stop, freeze with one foot gently on the ball.

blocks.title: Dribble through gates
activities: Dribble through two-marker gates at a comfortable pace.
Change direction after each gate and use both feet.

blocks.title: Finish with a goal game
activities: Score through a wide gate, collect the ball, and celebrate the attempt.
Keep turns short and finish while the player still feels fresh.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use wide gates and allow pauses whenever needed.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Add a simple colour or direction call before the player chooses a gate.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add a passive defender and scanning cue without raising physical intensity.

routines.title: Strong mover adventure
routines.purpose: Develop playful balance, crawling, rising, and landing control without external weights.

blocks.title: Animal trail
activities: Move like a bear, crab, or tall giraffe between two nearby markers.
Let the player choose the next movement.

blocks.title: Balance and rise
activities: Hold a stable support and balance briefly on each foot.
Sit to a safe low target and stand tall with control.

blocks.title: Soft landing statues
activities: Make a tiny two-foot jump and land quietly.
Freeze like a statue, then walk and repeat.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use hand support and very short movement distances.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use less hand support and add one reach while balancing.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: combine two movement patterns while keeping landings quiet and controlled.

routines.title: Quick feet, stop and smile
routines.purpose: Practise reacting, moving quickly for a few steps, and stopping under control.

blocks.title: Copy the leader
activities: Copy easy marching, side steps, and tiptoe movements.
Change the leader often.

blocks.title: Colour call starts
activities: The adult calls a marker colour and the player moves quickly toward it.
Keep each effort to a few seconds and walk fully back.

blocks.title: Run and freeze
activities: Move toward a gate, slow down before it, and freeze in balance.
Finish with an easy walk and breathing reset.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use one obvious direction and walking recovery.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use two possible directions and occasional ball carries.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add a visual cue and one controlled direction change.

routines.title: Play, move and pause
routines.purpose: Build comfortable activity through short football play and natural recovery, never running laps.

blocks.title: Treasure dribble
activities: Dribble to collect or touch a marker and return.
Walk whenever the player wants a break.

blocks.title: Short play rounds
activities: Alternate 30 seconds of ball play with 30–45 seconds of easy walking.
Complete four to six relaxed rounds.

blocks.title: Favourite move finish
activities: Let the player choose a favourite dribble, pass, or shot.
Stop while movement still looks comfortable.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use four rounds and unlimited walking breaks.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use up to six rounds while preserving the same relaxed pace.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add a simple choice during each play interval, not extra work time.

routines.title: All-round ball play
routines.purpose: Combine ball familiarity, balance, changing direction, and enjoyable movement.

blocks.title: Free ball play
activities: Explore different touches in a safe area.
The adult joins in with simple encouragement.

blocks.title: Move, balance, aim
activities: Dribble around a marker, balance briefly, then pass through a gate.
Alternate feet and keep the goal wide.

blocks.title: Player's choice
activities: Repeat the activity the player enjoyed most.
End with an easy walk and drink break.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use one activity at a time with plenty of space.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Link the dribble, balance, and pass into one simple journey.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add a choice of two routes while keeping instructions brief.

routines.title: Match confidence touches
routines.purpose: Rehearse first touch, scanning, and passing confidence while staying fresh.

blocks.title: Dynamic ball movement
activities: Move with the ball using both feet and gentle direction changes.
Gradually raise movement speed without sprinting.

blocks.title: Receive and choose
activities: Pass to a safe wall or partner and take the first touch toward one of two gates.
Look up before receiving and alternate feet.

blocks.title: Calm finishing
activities: Take a controlled first touch and pass or shoot through a wide target.
Finish with easy touches and breathing.

levelProgressions.beginner: Stop the ball when needed and use a wide target.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use two touches and let the partner call the target late.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: use a passive defender or tighter timing while preserving freshness.

routines.title: Body-control foundations
routines.purpose: Build supervised bodyweight squat, push, brace, balance, and landing technique.

blocks.title: Movement preparation
activities: March, side step, reach, and perform gentle ankle and hip movements.
Practise two quiet landings from a very small jump.

blocks.title: Controlled circuit
activities: Perform squat-to-target, incline push-up, dead bug, and supported balance.
Use one or two sets of six to ten clean repetitions and stop before technique changes.

blocks.title: Easy reset
activities: Walk easily and repeat comfortable mobility movements.
Tell the supervising adult about any discomfort.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use one set, high supports, and six controlled repetitions.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Add a second set or two repetitions, but not both in one session.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add coordination or range before any external resistance.

routines.title: React, accelerate and stop
routines.purpose: Develop short acceleration and safe stopping mechanics with complete recovery.

blocks.title: Rhythm and direction
activities: March, skip, and side step over short distances.
Build speed gradually and keep posture tall.

blocks.title: Quality efforts
activities: React to a visual call and accelerate for five to ten metres.
Slow down across several steps and walk back fully before repeating.

blocks.title: Walk and reset
activities: Walk for two to three minutes.
Finish when speed or stopping quality begins to drop.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use one direction and four total accelerations.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use two directions and up to six total accelerations.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add one decision or ball action before the acceleration.

routines.title: Ball interval games
routines.purpose: Build repeatable football movement with short ball rounds and visible recovery.

blocks.title: Ball and movement
activities: Use easy touches and turns between markers.
Include a drink and instruction break before the main rounds.

blocks.title: Work and recover
activities: Dribble, pass, or play a simple one-versus-one round for 30–45 seconds.
Walk and recover for at least the same amount of time; complete four to eight rounds.

blocks.title: Easy ball walk
activities: Walk with the ball and use relaxed touches.
Stop if technique or enjoyment drops.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use four rounds with 30 seconds work and 45 seconds recovery.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use six rounds with equal work and recovery.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: increase decision complexity, not total work and pace together.

routines.title: Football foundations
routines.purpose: Combine ball work, movement coordination, simple decisions, and an easy finish.

blocks.title: Fun activation
activities: Use a tag, mirror, or dribbling game with frequent role changes.
Keep everybody moving and avoid elimination.

blocks.title: Skill and movement mix
activities: Alternate a first-touch task, balance reach, and short dribble challenge.
Use short rounds and rotate the leading foot.

blocks.title: Game application
activities: Play a small target or scoring game with an adult or teammate.
Finish with an easy walk.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use predictable feeds and wide spaces.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Add a simple opponent or choice after control is consistent.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: combine scanning and a late decision in the game block.

routines.title: Technical match primer
routines.purpose: Prepare movement and sharpen familiar football actions without adding meaningful fatigue.

blocks.title: Dynamic technical activation
activities: Gradually progress from mobility and easy movement into ball touches.
Include passing, receiving, and changes of direction linked to the session theme.

blocks.title: Sharp, familiar actions
activities: Complete short passing-and-first-touch rounds with scanning.
Add three or four controlled five-metre accelerations with full walk-back recovery.

blocks.title: Finish fresh
activities: Use easy ball touches and walking.
End before movement quality falls.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use predictable service and extra setup time.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Add a late gate call or passive pressure.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add position-relevant scanning cues without extra volume.

routines.title: Football strength foundations
routines.purpose: Build controlled squat, lunge, push, pull-pattern, calf, and core foundations under qualified supervision.

blocks.title: Mobility and control
activities: Use dynamic ankle, hip, and upper-body movements.
Practise squat, hinge, and landing positions with no load.

blocks.title: Technique-first circuit
activities: Use squat-to-target, supported reverse lunge, incline push-up, calf raise, and dead bug.
Complete one or two sets of six to twelve repetitions with clean technique and comfortable effort.

blocks.title: Easy movement
activities: Walk and repeat comfortable mobility.
Record any exercise that needed an easier option.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use one set and the easiest stable variation.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use two sets; progress repetitions before resistance.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add an appropriate light resistance only after qualified technique review.

routines.title: Acceleration and stopping quality
routines.purpose: Practise short acceleration and deceleration while fresh, using full recovery and coach feedback.

blocks.title: Dynamic acceleration preparation
activities: Progress through mobility, marching, skipping, and two easy build-ups.
Raise intensity gradually.

blocks.title: Accelerate, then own the stop
activities: Complete four to six accelerations over eight to twelve metres.
Use full walk-back recovery, then practise lowering and stopping across several steps.

blocks.title: Walk down
activities: Walk easily for three minutes.
Stop the session if posture or braking quality declines.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use one start position and straight-line stopping.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Add one reaction cue or a gentle directional exit.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add a football decision before acceleration, not extra fatigue.

routines.title: Controlled football tempo
routines.purpose: Develop repeatable football movement through controlled ball intervals rather than all-out running.

blocks.title: Ball activation
activities: Use dynamic movement and progressive ball carries.
Rehearse the turns used in the main block at easy speed.

blocks.title: Tempo rounds
activities: Alternate 40–60 seconds of passing, dribbling, and changing direction with equal easy recovery.
Complete four to eight rounds at a sustainable pace.

blocks.title: Easy reset
activities: Walk with relaxed touches for four minutes.
Finish able to speak comfortably.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use four 40-second rounds with longer recovery.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use six rounds with equal work and recovery.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: increase football decisions before changing volume or pace.

routines.title: Complete football foundations
routines.purpose: Combine technical confidence, movement control, core strength, and short football efforts.

blocks.title: Technical activation
activities: Use dynamic mobility followed by ball touches and passing.
Keep the setup connected to the main theme.

blocks.title: Skill and athleticism
activities: Alternate a first-touch task with squat-to-target, dead bug, balance reach, and three short accelerations.
Keep rests generous enough for good technique.

blocks.title: Easy finish
activities: Walk and use relaxed ball touches.
Review one movement cue with the coach.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use fewer exercises and predictable technical feeds.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Add one tactical choice or second strength set.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: use position-aware choices while preserving the same workload ceiling.

routines.title: Freshness-first match primer
routines.purpose: Reinforce technical sharpness and a few fast actions without compromising match freshness.

blocks.title: Progressive activation
activities: Move from dynamic mobility into football-specific passing and receiving.
Increase intensity gradually but remain well below fatigue.

blocks.title: Position-relevant quality
activities: Use short first-touch, passing, or finishing combinations linked to the player's position.
Include three or four brief accelerations with full recovery.

blocks.title: Finish ready
activities: Use easy touches and walking.
End feeling sharper than at the start.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use familiar actions with predictable service.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Add a scanning call or passive pressure.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: increase perceptual demands without increasing volume.

routines.title: Compact football strength
routines.purpose: Develop supervised unilateral lower-body, push, pull, calf, and core strength that complements football.

blocks.title: Dynamic mobility microdose
activities: Prepare ankles, hips, trunk, and shoulders with controlled dynamic movement.
Rehearse each main pattern without resistance.

blocks.title: Football strength circuit
activities: Use split squat or supported lunge, hip hinge pattern, incline push-up, band row, calf raise, and dead bug.
Complete two sets of six to ten controlled repetitions with qualified feedback.

blocks.title: Reset and record
activities: Walk and use comfortable mobility.
Record technique notes before considering progression.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use bodyweight, stable supports, and one or two sets.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Progress range or repetitions before adding light resistance.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add small resistance increments after repeated technical competence and coach approval.

routines.title: Speed quality
routines.purpose: Train acceleration, braking, and a small number of direction changes while fully recovered.

blocks.title: Mobility and sprint preparation
activities: Progress from dynamic mobility into marching, skipping, and two build-ups.
Use coach feedback before faster work.

blocks.title: High-quality repetitions
activities: Complete four to eight accelerations over ten to fifteen metres with full recovery.
Add controlled deceleration; add at most one planned direction change.

blocks.title: Walk and finish
activities: Walk for three to five minutes.
Stop immediately if speed mechanics or control deteriorate.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use straight-line starts and four repetitions.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use varied starts and up to six quality repetitions.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: add a football perception cue before changing distance or volume.

routines.title: Repeat-effort football intervals
routines.purpose: Develop sustainable repeated football actions with controlled work-to-recovery ratios.

blocks.title: Progressive ball preparation
activities: Use dynamic movement, ball carries, and easy passing.
Build toward the main movement pattern over several minutes.

blocks.title: Football interval block
activities: Use passing, dribbling, or small-space football actions for 45–75 seconds.
Recover easily for at least 45–75 seconds and complete four to eight rounds.

blocks.title: Return to easy
activities: Walk with relaxed breathing and easy touches.
Do not add extra rounds after the planned finish.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use four short rounds and longer recovery.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use six rounds with equal work and recovery.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: change tactical complexity before increasing total load.

routines.title: Balanced football athleticism
routines.purpose: Combine football technique, mobility, unilateral control, core work, and short accelerations in a compact session.

blocks.title: Dynamic technical activation
activities: Use dynamic mobility followed by passing, receiving, and ball carries.
Keep the warm-up linked to the session.

blocks.title: High-value mixed block
activities: Alternate first-touch work with supported lunge, dead bug, balance reach, and four short accelerations.
Use generous rests and qualified technique feedback.

blocks.title: Easy review
activities: Walk and use easy mobility.
Record the main coaching cue and keep the next progression small.

levelProgressions.beginner: Use fewer activities and one strength set.
levelProgressions.intermediate: Use two strength sets or add a football decision, but not both.
levelProgressions.advanced: Research only: use position-aware decisions and controlled progression within the same duration ceiling.
